profiles.Summary: Factorio is a 2D top-down factory-building game with very modest GPU demands, and the Steam Deck handles it comfortably at native resolution and high settings even at low TDP. The main performance concern in large late-game factories is CPU simulation load (UPS), not GPU rendering, so frame rates remain stable for most of the game's progression.

MaxBattery.Notes: At 5 W TDP and a 30 fps lock the GPU is barely stressed for this 2D game, delivering excellent battery life. UPS may still drop in very large factories due to CPU simulation load, but GPU power draw stays minimal.

Optimal.Notes: Native resolution at 60 Hz looks sharp and crisp for this 2D game; the GPU is barely stressed so no upscaling is needed. CPU performance governs late-game smoothness — if UPS drops below 60 in a megabase, lower entity render distance and turn off lights.

profiles.Summary: Factorio is a 2D top-down strategy/simulation game with very modest GPU demands, running natively on Linux and verified on Steam Deck — it is primarily CPU-bound at large factory scales rather than GPU-bound. The game runs excellently on Deck at 60 fps in early-to-mid game, though very large late-game megabases with thousands of entities can stress the CPU and cause frame drops.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC requirements, Factorio's well-known CPU-bound simulation architecture, and the Deck hardware spec. On first run, check your UPS counter (F4 debug menu) in a busy area — if UPS drops below 60, the factory simulation itself is the bottleneck, not the graphics settings.

MaxBattery.Notes: Factorio is extremely light on the GPU; the TDP and clock limits here are to reduce power draw during long sessions. Battery life is excellent in early-to-mid game; a massive late-game factory will push CPU load and reduce battery life regardless of GPU settings.

KnownIssues: Late-game megabases with massive entity counts can drop the UPS/FPS below 60 regardless of graphics settings, as Factorio is heavily CPU-bound at scale.
The on-screen interface and text can be small at 1280x800; use the in-game UI scale setting to compensate.
Controller/gamepad support is functional but the game was designed for mouse and keyboard — some actions are less convenient on the Deck trackpads.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Factorio's GPU load is minimal even at max settings, so the Deck can sustain 60-90 fps easily in early-to-mid game; the frame rate ceiling in late game is set entirely by CPU simulation speed (UPS), not GPU. High sprite resolution uses more VRAM but is well within the Deck's 16 GB shared pool.
